patients.summary: Graphic designer in her late thirties with lifelong mild persistent asthma and atopic dermatitis who joins in 2023. Progressive dyspnea in 2024 leads to pulmonology, basilar emphysema and PiZZ alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency on weekly augmentation; in 2025 Raynaud-type episodes and hand stiffness lead to rheumatology and seropositive rheumatoid arthritis on hydroxychloroquine.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

36F graphic designer, works from home most days, moving her care here from her old practice. Main reason: wants one doctor she can reach. No acute concerns.

ASTHMA: had asthma as a kid, says she 'grew out of it' in high school, then it came back around 25 or so. Old PCP called it mild persistent and put her on fluticasone 110, 2 puffs BID; takes it every day, rinses after. Albuterol maybe once or twice a month, mostly with colds or cold air running. No nighttime symptoms, no ED visits or oral steroid bursts she can remember in years.

ECZEMA: lifelong, flares in the winter on the inner elbows and backs of knees. Triamcinolone cream BID during flares, a tube lasts her most of a winter.

PMH: asthma, atopic dermatitis.
PSH: T&A at age 7.
Meds: fluticasone HFA 110 mcg 2 puffs BID; albuterol HFA 2 puffs q4-6h prn; triamcinolone 0.1% cream BID prn flares.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: father had emphysema, diagnosed in his mid-40s. Mother has eczema. Maternal aunt with rheumatoid arthritis.
SH: never smoked, does not drink, no drugs. Lives in Holyoke. Graphic designer.
GYN: Pap with HPV last year at the old office, normal per pt.

ROS: no dyspnea at baseline, no chronic cough, no chest pain, no joint pain, no weight change. Otherwise negative.

EXAM: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: TMs clear, oropharynx clear, tonsils surgically absent.
Neck: supple, no adenopathy, no thyromegaly.
Lungs: clear, good air entry, no wheeze.
CV: RRR, no murmur.
Abd: soft, nontender.
Skin: mild dry patches antecubital fossae bilaterally, no excoriation or infection.
Ext: no edema.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
1. Mild persistent asthma: well controlled on current ICS. Continue fluticasone 110 2 puffs BID, albuterol prn. Asked her to let me know if she needs albuterol more than twice a week.
2. Atopic dermatitis: quiet now. Triamcinolone prn, emollients daily.
3. Health maintenance: baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, one-time HIV and HCV today. Flu vaccine given. Records request to prior practice for Pap and immunization dates. COVID booster when the new formula is out.

RTC for physical in the spring.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Megan, your labs from Tuesday are back. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests, and cholesterol all look good, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. Welcome to the practice.

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Summary
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records received from prior primary care office (fax, 9 pages, mostly visit stubs and medication lists).

Summary abstracted by MA:
- Asthma: childhood asthma per history; symptoms recurred in her mid-twenties and she was treated as mild persistent asthma, on fluticasone HFA 110 mcg 2 puffs BID with albuterol prn since then.
- Eczema: triamcinolone 0.1% cream prn.
- Pap with HPV co-test 03/2022: NILM, HPV negative.
- Tdap 04/2019.
- Allergies: NKDA.

No PFTs or imaging in the packet. Scanned to media.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for 2023-24 COVID vaccine. No fever today, no prior reactions beyond a sore arm. Pfizer 0.3 mL IM L deltoid, lot logged. Waited 15 min, fine. Card updated.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Pharmacy fax: fluticasone HFA 110 mcg, no refills left. Last seen 9/12/23, on med list, controlled. Routed to PCP.

PCP: approved, 90-day supply with 3 refills.

documents.title: Eczema cream
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my eczema has been bad this winter, mostly both elbows and behind my knees, itchy at night. I'm almost out of the triamcinolone. Could you send a new tube? Sorry I cancelled last month, deadline week.

documents.title: RE: Eczema cream
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No problem at all. I sent a larger tube of the triamcinolone to your pharmacy. Twice a day on the patches for up to two weeks, then back off, and keep a thick moisturizer on after showers. If it looks weepy, crusted or isn't settling in two weeks, send a photo or come in. We'll catch up at your physical in May.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT

S: 37F feeling well. Asthma: daily fluticasone, albuterol a handful of times since the fall, none in the past month. Eczema calmed down once the heat came on less, using the cream rarely now. Sleeping OK, busy with freelance work on top of her job. Walks most evenings.

Meds: fluticasone HFA 110 2 puffs BID, albuterol prn, triamcinolone cream prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol.

ROS: no cough, no exertional dyspnea, no wheeze at night, no joint complaints. Negative otherwise.

Exam: NAD.
HEENT normal. Neck no nodes or thyroid enlargement.
Lungs clear bilaterally, no wheeze.
Heart regular, no murmurs.
Abdomen soft, no masses.
Skin: a few faint dry patches L antecubital, otherwise clear.
Ext warm, no edema.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
- Health maintenance: Pap/HPV 2022 normal, next due 2027. Tdap 2019. Flu and COVID up to date for the season. CBC and CMP today.
- Asthma: controlled, no change.
- Eczema: emollients, cream prn.

Return in a year, sooner prn.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Megan, your blood count and chemistry panel from the physical are normal. Have a good summer.

orders.reason: Progressive exertional dyspnea and chronic productive cough despite ICS

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 37F with asthma here because her breathing has been getting worse since around early June. Notices it walking up the hill to the bus and carrying groceries up to her apartment, has stopped her evening walks the last few weeks. Coughs every day now, brings up clear phlegm, worse in the mornings. No fever, no chest pain, no hemoptysis, no leg swelling, no weight loss. Says she has not missed fluticasone doses. Albuterol now a few times a week, helps a little but not like it used to. No sick contacts. No new pets, no mold at home, no change at work (desk job). Never smoked, no vaping.

FHx reviewed: father with emphysema in his 40s.

O: comfortable at rest, speaks full sentences.
Lungs: air movement fair, prolonged expiratory phase, no crackles, no focal findings.
CV: regular, no murmur, no JVD.
Ext: no edema, no clubbing.

A/P
1. Progressive exertional dyspnea and daily productive cough in an adherent asthmatic, several months, never smoker. Not behaving like her usual asthma. Referring to pulmonology for full evaluation including PFTs and imaging; asked them to see her soon. Continue fluticasone and albuterol in the meantime; ED or call if dyspneic at rest.
2. Flu vaccine given today.

RTC after pulmonology.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: 2024-25 COVID vaccine, Moderna 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. Pt asked about pulmonology wait; front desk called referral line, appt 12/4. Observed 15 min, no reaction.

conditions.label: Emphysema
conditions.note: Basilar-predominant on chest x-ray at pulmonology

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 12/04/2024
Referred by: primary care

Thank you for sending Ms. Larkin, a 37-year-old never smoker with asthma, for evaluation of worsening breathlessness.

She describes half a year of steadily increasing shortness of breath and a daily cough raising clear sputum, despite taking her inhaled fluticasone faithfully. No smoking history and no occupational dust or fume exposure. Her father was diagnosed with emphysema at 44.

Medications: fluticasone HFA 110 mcg 2 puffs twice daily; albuterol HFA as needed; triamcinolone cream for eczema.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: breath sounds diminished at both bases with a prolonged expiratory phase.

Data:
- CBC within normal limits.
- Chest radiograph: hyperinflated lungs with emphysematous change most marked at the bases.
- Spirometry: FEV1/FVC 65% (normal >70%), consistent with obstruction; minimal response to bronchodilator.

Impression: fixed airflow obstruction with lower-zone emphysema in a young never smoker with a father who had early emphysema. This pattern raises strong concern for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. A serum alpha-1 antitrypsin level was drawn today and is pending; we will phenotype if it is low.

Plan: continue current inhalers. Will call her with results and see her back in about six weeks with full PFTs.

Pulmonology

conditions.label: Alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency
conditions.note: PiZZ per pulmonology; level and phenotype copy requested

documents.title: Alpha-1 results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the lung doctor's office called yesterday. They said my alpha-1 level is really low and the genetic type came back ZZ, so I have alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. I see them again in January. I'm honestly a little freaked out and wondering if this is what my dad had. Can we talk about it before then?

documents.title: RE: Alpha-1 results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Megan, thank you for letting me know, and I'm sorry, that is a lot to take in right before the holidays. It does explain the breathing changes, and it is very possible it is what your father had. There is treatment for this and pulmonology will walk you through it. I've asked their office to fax the results to us. Let's sit down early January; the front desk will reach out with a time. Keep using your inhalers as you have been.

documents.title: Outside Lab Results
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Fax from pulmonology office, 2 pages: serum alpha-1 antitrypsin 21 mg/dL (ref 100-190), collected 12/04/2024; alpha-1 antitrypsin phenotype PiZZ, reported 12/19/2024. Scanned and routed to PCP.

PCP: reviewed. Consistent with what pt reported. Visit set for 1/8.

events.reason: New diagnosis of alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, PiZZ, baseline liver imaging

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here to talk through the new alpha-1 diagnosis. Pulmonology saw her 12/4 for the dyspnea: basilar emphysema on CXR, obstruction on spirometry with little bronchodilator response. AAT level came back 21 mg/dL, phenotype PiZZ (fax 1/6). She has pulm follow-up 1/22 for full PFTs. Breathing about the same as the fall, cough with clear sputum most mornings. Still on fluticasone BID and albuterol a few times a week. Has been reading online and is worried about her liver and about what this means for work and the long term. She thinks her father's emphysema was probably the same thing; he was never tested that she knows of.

O: comfortable, no accessory muscle use.
Lungs: diminished at the bases, prolonged expiration, no wheeze.
CV regular. Abd soft, liver not palpable below the costal margin, no splenomegaly. No jaundice. No clubbing or edema.

A/P
1. Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, PiZZ, with emphysema. Explained the lung and liver sides of this in plain terms. Pulmonology will discuss augmentation therapy at her next visit. From our side: vaccines to protect lungs and liver, a baseline liver panel and abdominal ultrasound, and absolute smoke avoidance, which she already does. Gave her the patient foundation's information sheet. Mentioned that blood relatives can be tested if they want to be, through their own doctors.
2. Vaccines today: PCV20, hepatitis A #1, Heplisav-B #1. Heplisav #2 in one month, hep A #2 in six months.
3. Asthma: no change to inhalers pending pulmonology.

RTC in spring or after pulm, sooner if worse.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 01/22/2025

Ms. Larkin returns after her alpha-1 testing: serum level 21 mg/dL, PiZZ.

Complete PFTs: post-bronchodilator FEV1 58% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.65; DLCO 63% predicted.
CT chest: panlobular emphysema with lower-lobe predominance. No pulmonary nodules. No bronchiectasis.
Serum IgA 210 mg/dL, normal.

Assessment: severe alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (ZZ) with emphysema and moderate airflow obstruction.

Plan:
- Start weekly intravenous alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor 60 mg/kg through a home-infusion service; benefits investigation and authorization under way.
- Continue fluticasone and albuterol as prescribed.
- Hepatitis A and B and pneumococcal vaccination through primary care.
- Liver tests yearly and a baseline liver ultrasound, also through primary care.
- No exposure to tobacco smoke.
- Return in about six months.

Pulmonology

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Heplisav-B dose 2 of 2, 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Tolerated dose 1 without issue. Reminded about hep A #2 in July and her ultrasound on 2/19 (nothing to eat after midnight).

events.reason: Baseline liver imaging, alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency

reports.text: Indication: alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, PiZZ; baseline. Technique: grayscale and color Doppler of the upper abdomen. Liver: normal in size, measuring 14.1 cm in the midclavicular line, with smooth contour and normal homogeneous echotexture. No focal hepatic lesion. Hepatic and portal veins patent with normal flow direction. Gallbladder without stones or wall thickening. Common bile duct 3 mm. Pancreas partly obscured by bowel gas, visualized portions normal. Spleen normal at 9.8 cm. Both kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Normal abdominal ultrasound. No sonographic evidence of liver disease.

documents.title: Liver results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Megan, good news: your liver blood tests are all normal and the ultrasound shows a normal-sized, healthy-looking liver with no masses. We'll repeat the liver tests once a year. Pulmonology's note came through too, so I know they're arranging the weekly infusions.

documents.title: Home Infusion Pharmacy
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Call from home-infusion specialty pharmacy coordinating weekly alpha-1 augmentation ordered by pulmonology. Insurance approval received. Requested PCP contact info, current med list, allergy status and recent weight. Gave NKDA, weight 61 kg at 1/8 visit, med list as on file. First nurse home visit planned for 3/11. They will fax a start-of-care notice.

medications.sig: 60 mg/kg IV once weekly by home infusion

documents.title: Home Infusion Start of Care
documents.author: home infusion pharmacy
documents.body:
START OF CARE NOTICE
Patient: Megan Larkin
Therapy: alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor (human), 60 mg/kg IV weekly; ordering provider pulmonology.
First infusion given at home 03/11/2025 by infusion RN via peripheral IV, completed without reaction. Vital signs stable before and after. Patient taught signs of infusion reaction. Weekly visits scheduled.
This notice is for the primary care record.

medications.sig: Take 1 to 2 tablets by mouth every 6 to 8 hours as needed for joint pain, no more than 1200 mg per day

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

S: 38F. Alpha-1 (PiZZ) with emphysema, on weekly home augmentation since March, no reactions; the infusion nurse comes Tuesday evenings. Feels her breathing is a bit better than in the winter, back to short walks, still a morning cough. Fluticasone BID, albuterol a couple of times a week. Eczema quiet.

New: for about a month her hands ache and feel stiff when she gets up, loosens up after she gets going. Thinks it's from long days on the tablet and mouse. Taking OTC ibuprofen 200 mg, 1-2 tabs every 6-8 h on the bad days, never more than 6 a day.

Meds: fluticasone HFA 110 2 puffs BID; albuterol prn; triamcinolone cream prn; alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor 60 mg/kg IV weekly (pulm); ibuprofen OTC prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol.
PHQ-2: 1.

Exam: well appearing.
Lungs: diminished at bases, prolonged expiration, no wheeze.
Heart regular, no murmur.
Abd soft, no hepatosplenomegaly.
Hands: full range of motion, grip intact.
Skin clear.
Ext: no edema.

A/P
1. Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with emphysema: on augmentation, followed by pulm. CMP today for yearly liver check.
2. Asthma: unchanged regimen.
3. Hand aches/stiffness, about a month: likely overuse from work. OK to use ibuprofen as she is, with food, within the daily max. Ergonomics. Let me know if it lasts or spreads.
4. Health maintenance: hep A #2 due July, booked. Pap/HPV due 2027. CBC, CMP.

RTC 1 year, sooner prn.

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 11/24/2025

Reason for referral: cold-induced finger color change and joint symptoms.

History: 38-year-old woman with mild persistent asthma, atopic dermatitis and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency on augmentation. For roughly half a year her fingers blanch and then turn blue on cold exposure or under stress; the attacks hurt and sometimes tingle. Intermittent pain and morning stiffness in the hands and knees over the same period. Family history: father with emphysema at 44, a maternal aunt with RA, mother with eczema. No tobacco, alcohol or drug use.

Medications: fluticasone, albuterol prn, triamcinolone cream, ibuprofen prn, weekly alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: vitals normal. Both hands show fingertip pallor; no digital ulcers, no gangrene; capillary refill under 2 seconds. Remainder of the examination unremarkable.

Laboratory (drawn at visit): CBC normal. ESR 50 mm/hr (0-20). CRP 24 mg/L (<10). ANA positive. Anti-centromere negative. Anti-Scl-70 negative. RF positive. Anti-CCP positive.

Assessment:
1. Rheumatoid arthritis, seropositive (RF and anti-CCP), with elevated inflammatory markers.
2. Raynaud phenomenon. Negative scleroderma-associated antibodies and no features of systemic sclerosis on exam.

Plan (discussed by phone 12/02/2025):
- Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily. Chosen as initial therapy in view of her lung disease and PiZZ status.
- Baseline eye examination within the first year.
- Raynaud: warm gloves, layered clothing, avoid cold exposure; no medication at this time.
- Ibuprofen as needed may continue.
- Return in about 4 months.

Rheumatology

documents.title: Eye Examination Report
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
EYE EXAMINATION
Date of exam: 01/13/2026
Reason: baseline screening before long-term hydroxychloroquine (started 12/2025 by rheumatology).

Visual acuity 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS with correction. Pupils equal, no afferent defect. Intraocular pressures normal. Anterior segments quiet. Dilated fundus exam: healthy optic nerves, maculae flat with normal foveal reflex, vessels and periphery normal OU.
Automated 10-2 visual fields: full OU, reliable.
SD-OCT macula: normal retinal layers OU, no parafoveal thinning.

Impression: normal baseline exam, no evidence of hydroxychloroquine retinal toxicity.
Plan: annual screening beginning after 5 years of use, sooner if visual symptoms.

Ophthalmology
